newsitem.title: FRANCE: Murdered girls' funeral draws 5,000 in France.
newsitem.headline: Murdered girls' funeral draws 5,000 in France.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe joined 5,000 mourners on Thursday at the funeral of four girls raped and slain last week in a crime that sparked calls for the return of the guillotine.
The ceremony took place in the cathedral of the Channel port of Boulogne-sur-Mer as the National Assembly in Paris suspended its session for 10 minutes to honour the victims.

Peggy, 20, her 17-year-old sister Amelie, Isabelle, 20, and her sister Audrey, 17, went missing on the night of February 11 during carnival celebrations. Their costumed bodies were found days later hastily buried in the sand near a World War Two concrete bunker.
Two scrap metal dealer brothers, one a convicted murderer and the other a convicted rapist, are in custody on suspicion of raping and strangling the girls.

In the wake of a series of sex killings and Belgium's child murder scandal, the government has proposed a bill to toughen punishment of sex offenders and introduce medical tracking of rapists after their release from prison.
The killings also led to calls for a reintroduction of the death penalty. The guillotine was abolished in 1981.
